subject: Urgent: Hosted inference slowdown impacting NovaCorp (EU)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Dunn <alicia.dunn@novacorp.com>, support@novacorp.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: Elevated latency and partial failures in EU hosted inference

Hi Alicia / NovaCorp team,

I wanted to quickly surface an incident we are actively investigating. Starting at ~08:00 UTC we observed elevated P95/P99 latency and a small percentage of 503 responses for hosted inference endpoints in our eu-west-1 region that can impact generation and chat flows. Our monitoring shows affected requests are primarily going to the model pool used by your account.

Immediate notes: 
- Impact: generation latency spiking to 3–7s P95 and occasional 503s for some requests
- Scope: a subset of EU customers (we believe NovaCorp traffic is within the impacted pool)
- Action: engineering and SRE are on the bridge; we are prioritizing routing and cache reconciliation to reduce tail latency

We will post updates to our status page and follow up with a mitigation plan shortly. Apologies for the disruption — I know this affects your demo traffic.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops-bridge-log-snippet.txt (text), p95-latency-graph.png (image)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 08:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: Elevated latency and partial failures in EU hosted inference

On Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 08:12, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> I wanted to quickly surface an incident we are actively investigating.

Evelyn — we have an SRE bridge (https://ops-bridge.redwood.ai/bridges/ops-20260205-eu) and initial triage shows a cache-coherence issue in our per-prefix KV cache that caused frequent cache misses followed by cold-priming on hot prefixes. That increases per-request work and lengthens the tail. A small subset of requests also hit a transient request queue overflow which returned 503s.

Current mitigation steps underway (in-progress):
1) Temporarily enable additional worker capacity in eu-west-1 for affected model-pool (rolling upscales now).
2) Flushing and repairing prefix caches on a per-pool basis to avoid large simultaneous priming waves.
3) Route critical customer prefixes to a fallback stable model-variant that has larger cache residency until the cache is healthy.

I will post bridge notes and log snippets to the status page entry. Recommend an initial customer email acknowledging the incident and the short-term mitigations; operations will follow with an ETA for full root-cause analysis.

— Irene
Principal SRE

Attachments: ops-bridge-log-snippet.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Dunn <alicia.dunn@novacorp.com>, support@novacorp.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: Update: mitigation in place for EU slowdown — steps for NovaCorp

Hi Alicia,

Quick update from our ops team following the initial alert:

What we did (10:00 UTC):
- Increased worker capacity in the eu-west-1 pool servicing NovaCorp routes (visible improvement in throughput)
- Applied targeted prefix-cache repairs and moved your critical prefixes to a fallback model-variant to reduce cache misses
- Implemented short-term rate smoothing for bursty keys to prevent queue overflow

What you may see now:
- Reduced P95 latency (we expect numbers to fall back towards baseline over the next 30–90 minutes)
- Intermittent 503s should be greatly reduced; if you continue to see errors please forward logs to support@redwood.com with the request IDs

Next steps:
- We will run a controlled verification for a full cache reconciliation and performance test.
- Engineering will provide an RCA and long-term remediation plan within 72 hours.
- Customer success (Karthik) will follow up on any business impact and credits.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate you flagging this quickly. I will keep you posted as we progress.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Related status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-05-eu-degrade

A couple of follow-ups:
- We will proactively apply a one-time service credit for the affected window (DC-8741). I will email the paperwork/ordering link after we confirm the exact impacted API token window with you.
- If NovaCorp wants a temporary capacity reservation while we complete the RCA, we can provision a short-term Dedicated pool for the affected model routes (sales can fast-track approval).

Alicia — do you have any remaining customer-facing concerns I should address in the follow-up? We want to ensure your demo runs tomorrow without surprises.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
